## Why Equations and Reproducible Reporting Matter

Multilevel models are typically taught through level-by-level notation before
they are taught through R formula syntax. `mlmr` connects the fitted `lme4`
formula, level-by-level equations, combined mixed-model equation, labeled Tau
covariance matrices, APA tables, effect sizes, and reproducible R code.

## Level-by-Level Equations and Coefficient Key

`mlmr` assigns predictors to levels from the fitted data: a predictor constant
within every unit of a grouping factor is placed at that cluster level, while
cross-level interactions enter the equation for the lower-level slope they
moderate:

```{r equations-example, eval = TRUE}
library(mlmr)

dat <- example_hsb(n_schools = 12, min_students = 10, max_students = 14)
spec <- mlm_spec(
  outcome = "mathscore",
  fixed = list(
    ses = list(center = "CWC"),
    meanses = list(center = "GMC"),
    sector = list(center = "none")
  ),
  grouping = list(schoolid = "schoolid"),
  random = list(schoolid = list(
    intercept = TRUE, slopes = "ses", correlation = TRUE
  )),
  interactions = list(c("ses", "sector")),
  data = dat
)
result <- suppressWarnings(mlm_fit(spec))
eq <- mlm_latex_equations(result)
eq$level
writeLines(strsplit(eq$equations[[2]], "\\\\ ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
```

The coefficient key links each equation symbol to its fitted estimate and notes
whether the corresponding coefficient carries a random effect or moderates a
random slope:

```{r equations-key, eval = TRUE}
eq$key
```

## Effect Sizes, Reliability, and APA Tables

In addition to APA fixed-effects, dummy-coding, variance-component, and Gaussian
ICC tables, `mlmr` computes marginal and conditional $R^2$ (Nakagawa, Johnson, &
Schielzeth, 2017) and HLM-style empirical Bayes random-intercept reliability
(Raudenbush & Bryk, 2002):

```{r reporting-helpers, eval = TRUE}
mlm_r2(result)
mlm_reliability(result)
```

When `lmerTest` is installed, passing `df_method = "satterthwaite"` (or
`"kenward-roger"` with `pbkrtest`) adds denominator degrees of freedom and
$t$-based intervals to Gaussian APA tables.

## Publication Bundle Archive

For manuscript supplements and open-science repositories,
`mlm_write_publication_bundle()` packages the Quarto report, standalone R
script, raw LaTeX (`amsmath` + `graphicx`), HTML/Word APA tables,
reproducibility checklist CSV, and software version table into a single `.zip`
archive:

```{r bundle-example, eval = FALSE}
mlm_write_publication_bundle(result, "mlmr_publication_bundle.zip")
```

Software citations can also be generated directly:

```{r software, eval = TRUE}
mlm_software_apa()
```
